title: 5 things to know about Nam Ji-hyun, the star of "Make Me Tingle" - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao October 21, 2026 Nam Ji-hyun is back with another unconventional romance in "Make Me Tingle." Starring opposite Kim Jae-young, she plays Gong Yeon-su, a conservative marketer who unexpectedly reunites with the free-spirited CEO of a sex toy start-up after an awkward blind date. As their contrasting views on love lead to plenty of disagreements, romance slowly begins to blossom. But there's much more to Nam than her on-screen charm. From growing up in the spotlight to her academic pursuits and life off-screen, here are five things worth knowing about the actress 
 She has been acting since she was a child
 Photo: Instagram @hyuniiiiiii_95917
 Nam Ji-hyun has practically grown up in front of the camera. Born in 1995, she made her acting debut at just eight years old in the 2004 drama Say You Love Me . She soon became a familiar face on Korean television, often playing younger versions of leading actresses in dramas such as East of Eden (2008), Queen Seondeok (2009) and Will It Snow for Christmas? (2009). Her talent didn't go unnoticed either, earning her Best Young Actress honours at the MBC Drama Awards in both 2008 and 2009.
 Shopping King Louie helped her move beyond her child-actress image
 Photo: MBC
 Making the transition from child actress to leading lady isn't always easy, but Shopping King Louie (2016) marked a turning point for Nam at 21. Starring opposite Seo In-guk, she played Go Bok-shil, a kind-hearted young woman who crosses paths with a wealthy heir suffering from amnesia. Nam later shared that she hoped the romantic comedy had convinced audiences she could take on adult roles, though she modestly rated her own performance just 70 out of 100. The drama paved the way for popular romances like Suspicious Partner (2017) and 100 Days My Prince (2018).

 She has quietly become an awards regular
 Photo: Instagram @hyuniiiiiii_95917
 With more than two decades in the industry, Nam has picked up quite a collection of acting accolades along the way. She won her first Best Young Actress award at the 2006 SBS Drama Awards for My Love , followed by Best New Actress at the 2016 MBC Drama Awards for Shopping King Louie and a Top Excellence Award for 365: Repeat the Year (2020). More recently, her portrayal of rookie divorce lawyer Han Yu-ri alongside Jang Na-ra in Good Partner (2024) earned her another Top Excellence Award at the SBS Drama Awards.
 She studied psychology to better understand her characters
 Photo: Instagram @hyuniiiiiii_95917
 While many actors choose to study theatre or film, Nam took a different path. An academically gifted student who ranked among the top five in high school, she enrolled at Sogang University in 2014 to study psychology, graduating in 2020 while juggling her acting career. Having spent years analysing characters, she wanted to better understand human behaviour and emotions. Interestingly, during a recent appearance on Yoo Jae-suk's Whenever Possible , she joked that people often expect her to read their minds, something she readily admitted she has no idea how to do.
 She is a devoted cat mum
 Photo: Instagram @hyuniiiiiii_95917
 When she's not busy filming, Nam has two furry companions waiting for her at home, or at least she did when she first introduced them to fans. The actress is a devoted cat mum to Tancookie and Mone, whom she has previously shown off on social media. She even created a dedicated Instagram account for the pair, sharing adorable snaps of their everyday antics. It's a sweet glimpse into her life away from the cameras, especially for fans more accustomed to seeing her navigate complicated relationships and emotional storylines on screen.
